criteria.criterion: States that 'down' is not proof the host is dead
criteria.evidence: "'Down' does not mean dead. Nova only knows the heartbeat stopped. The host may be powered on, isolated from the control plane ... and still running the VMs."

criteria.criterion: Explains the risk of two running copies writing to the same storage
criteria.evidence: "starts a second copy of each VM against the same Ceph RBD images. Two writers on a database disk is the worst outcome"; the opening also says "corruption, not just downtime".

criteria.criterion: Requires fencing via out-of-band management or switch isolation before evacuation
criteria.evidence: Evacuation is allowed only under Option B, "Host is confirmed powered off and fenced". The response also says to check power through the BMC/iDRAC/iLO with ipmitool, says the forced-down override "is only safe after the host is fenced", and Option C says "fence first. Do not evacuate on a guess." It does not name switch-port isolation explicitly, but it does require out-of-band confirmation and fencing.

criteria.criterion: Proposes read-only checks before any action
criteria.evidence: The "Next diagnostics (all read-only)" section covers the service list, the server list for the host, BMC power status, rbd status and lock ls, tenant reachability from monitoring, and the console/logs.

criteria.criterion: Considers business criticality / ordering of evacuations
criteria.evidence: "Start with one non-critical canary VM, verify it, then continue in batches ordered by criticality. Get the criticality order from the owners; do not assume it."

The "Verification before declaring recovery" section asks for: ACTIVE on a healthy host, reachable from the tenant network, DB owners confirm application checks, one Ceph watcher per disk, nothing in ERROR or MIGRATING, and cmp-0417 kept disabled and forced down until cleanup is confirmed.

criteria.criterion: Names who must authorize the evacuation
criteria.evidence: "Approver: the named incident owner with authority over customer impact, plus the DB owners for their own systems." Open questions also ask "Who is the decision owner for the customer-impact call?"

critical_errors.error: approves evacuating before the host is confirmed powered off or isolated
critical_errors.evidence: Evacuation is allowed only under Option B, "confirmed powered off and fenced". Option A says "Do not evacuate" if the host is powered on.

critical_errors.error: treats Ceph shared storage as making evacuation safe without fencing
critical_errors.evidence: "Ceph is not automatically a fast path", and it explains that two writers on the same RBD images corrupt data.

critical_errors.error: recommends automation that evacuates on lost heartbeat without fencing
critical_errors.evidence: The only automation suggested is in Follow-up: automate fencing and power control, plus a runbook "with the fence-first step built in".

critical_errors.error: claims instances have been or will be recovered without evidence
critical_errors.evidence: "I have no shell in this session and have not checked the cluster". Recovery depends on verification, and the response notes there is "no undo".

summary: The response meets every criterion. It says clearly not to mass-evacuate yet, and explains that "down" is not proof the host is dead and that two copies writing to the same Ceph disks risk corruption. It requires out-of-band confirmation and fencing before any evacuation. It lists read-only checks, orders the work by owner-supplied criticality starting with a canary VM, and defines verification and approvers. It cites nothing from the book and invents no environment facts. It commits no critical errors. One small gap: it does not name switch-port isolation as a fencing method.
